children: Indonesia's central bank held its benchmark interest rate steady but raised its deposit facility rate Wednesday, as the threat of an MSCI market downgrade fueled capital outflows and pressured the rupiah.

Bank Indonesia kept its benchmark seven-day reverse repo rate at 5.75%, as seven of nine economists polled by The Wall Street Journal had expected. Two had forecast a quarter-percentage-point increase.

The central bank raised its overnight deposit facility rate by a quarter percentage point to 5.0%, increasing the return banks receive on funds placed with it overnight. It kept its lending facility rate at 6.50%.
The decision is aimed at stabilizing the rupiah, attracting foreign capital inflows and keeping inflation within the central bank's target range, Gov. Destry Damayanti said at a press conference.
The moves come as investors assess MSCI's proposal to downgrade Indonesia's equity market, citing transparency concerns. The index provider is expected to announce its final decision in June 2027.

A downgrade from emerging-market to standalone status would exclude Indonesian equities from MSCI's main indexes tracked by global funds. The proposal sparked a sharp selloff, with Indonesian stocks posting their steepest drop since the 1998 Asian financial crisis.
The downgrade threat also fueled selling in bonds and accelerated capital outflows, adding pressure on Bank Indonesia to shore up the currency.

Deteriorating investor sentiment, elevated energy prices, renewed fiscal risks and tighter global monetary conditions could prompt a quarter-percentage-point rate increase in November, CIMB analysts said in a recent note.
